title: BackedEnum::tryFrom() is nullable, but not for a known backing literal

ground_truth.statement: BackedEnum::tryFrom() returns the case when the backing value is known and null otherwise. The fixture passes the literal 'active', which is Status::Active's backing value, so the result of that call is never null and passing it to the Status parameter is sound; passing the result of tryFrom($raw) for an arbitrary string is not, because that value can be null. The runtime script decides both directions: tryFrom('active') is Status::Active, tryFrom('nope') is null and label(null) throws a TypeError, while from('nope') throws ValueError instead of returning null.

notes: PHPStan 2.3.1 models tryFrom() conditionally on a literal argument and reports only the genuinely nullable call (line 25) - a correct row. Psalm 6.20.0 and Mago 1.57.0 report PossiblyNullArgument / possibly-null-argument on line 20 as well, where the runtime proof shows the value is Status::Active and can never be null; that report is the recorded false positive, and the forbidden predicate keeps the case honest instead of quietly widening the expectation. The line-20 claim is not a missing optional warning: the value is not merely usually non-null, it is decidable from the literal and the enum's backing values. PHPStan's own fixture tests/PHPStan/Analyser/nsrt/enums.php models the call with a variable subject as 'X|null', which is why the switch to a literal matters here.

sources.note: PHPStan asserts tryFrom() returns X|null for a variable subject
